name: Turkey Taco Rice Skillet
intro_html: All the flavor of taco night, built for the week ahead. Lean ground turkey, rice, black beans, and corn get a taco-seasoned kick and a melt of cheddar. It is filling, high in protein, and it reheats like a dream. Scoop it into a bowl, over lettuce, or into a tortilla, and you have lunch handled for days.
ingredients_display: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans, drained (910 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 5 cups, drained (840 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (~7 oz) (196 g)
Chicken Broth (Swanson): 3 cups (to cook rice in-pan) (2000 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 3.5 cups dry jasmine: ~$0.86. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Seasoned Black Beans, 4 cans, drained: ~$5.94. Buy 4 cans: $6.66.
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 5 cups, drained: ~$1.59. Buy 2 cans: $1.64.
Fat Free Cheddar, about 1 3/4 cups shredded (~7 oz): ~$1.94. Buy 1 8oz bag: $2.25.
Salsa, 1 cup chunky tomato salsa (per 4): ~$3.69. Buy 2 16oz jars: $3.94.
Chicken Broth, 3 cups (to cook rice in-pan): ~$3.04. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 3 32oz cartons.
Pantry seasonings (taco seasoning): ~$0.52. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $34.00 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.43 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $37.61 across 14 servings, roughly $2.69 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $7.80 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $45.41. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) versus $11 or more for a fast-casual burrito bowl. Catch turkey on sale and it drops further.
shop_smart: Turkey and beef are interchangeable here. Whichever is cheaper that week wins. Turkey runs leaner, beef runs a touch cheaper on sale.
Buy the ground meat on sale and freeze it in one-pound packs. Same rule that makes every batch cheaper over time.
Beans and corn by the case are pennies cheaper per can and you will use them again next week.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice in the chicken broth instead of water, three and a half cups dry jasmine per the package, then set aside.
Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet with the olive oil over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the taco seasoning, the salsa, and a splash of water and stir until coated.
Drain and rinse the beans and corn, then warm them through.
Combine the rice, turkey, beans, and corn in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded cheddar.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice in the chicken broth and set aside.
